cards.explanation: The answer is neither cold nor hot. Jesus says, "I know your deeds; you are neither cold nor hot." Then He adds, "How I wish you were one or the other!" (Revelation 3:15)

The answer is that He is about to vomit them out of His mouth. That's a strong picture. He says, "So because you are lukewarm—neither hot nor cold—I am about to vomit you out of My mouth!" I think this is one of those lines you read once and sit with for a minute. It's heavy, and it comes right after He says He wishes they were hot or cold.

The answer is poor. Laodicea says, "I am rich; I have grown wealthy and need nothing." Jesus answers that they don't realize they are "…wretched, pitiful, poor, blind, and naked." That's a big gap between what they say about themselves and what He sees.

The answer is gold refined by fire. Jesus says, "I counsel you to buy from Me gold refined by fire so that you may become rich…" They said they were rich, and He tells them how to actually become rich. And notice who they're buying it from. It's from Him.

The answer is clothed. Jesus counsels them to buy "…white garments so that you may be clothed and your shameful nakedness not exposed…" They were called naked a verse earlier. Now He points them to the clothes.
The answer is True. Jesus says they are "blind," and then counsels them to buy "…salve to anoint your eyes so that you may see." He doesn't just name the problem. He offers the fix.

The answer is those He loves. Jesus says, "Those I love I rebuke and discipline." That changes how the hard words sound, friends. He's saying them to people He loves, and they're not coming from a stranger.

The answer is True. Right after He says He rebukes and disciplines those He loves, Jesus says, "Therefore be earnest and repent." It's a direct word to the church in Laodicea. And it follows right behind the love.

The answer is False. Jesus says, "Behold, I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears My voice and opens the door, I will come in and dine with him, and he with Me." The word is anyone, friends. He doesn't limit it to the leaders.

The answer is that He will come in and dine with them. Jesus says, "…I will come in and dine with him, and he with Me." He comes inside to share a meal with them. I love that, because a meal is where people really stay a while.

The answer is the right to sit with Him on His throne. Jesus says, "To the one who overcomes, I will grant the right to sit with Me on My throne, just as I overcame and sat down with My Father on His throne." That is a BIG promise, friends. And it comes to a church He just called lukewarm.
